claim: Buddhist images use hand gestures (mudras) as a semantic iconographic vocabulary: raised open palms can signify protection (abhaya), joined thumb and index finger teaching, two-handed dharmachakra the teaching/first-sermon association, and nested palms in the lap meditation (dhyana). Sri Lankan Buddha sculptures documented from the Anuradhapura/Polonnaruwa traditions through Kandy use this wider South Asian vocabulary, notably vitarka and abhaya.
bounded_by: This establishes the iconographic vocabulary and its Sri Lankan use, not the exact identification, date, museum location or distinctness of the eight Run28 photographed statues. GF-MUDRA-04 remains unresolved.
notes: Reader use: teach how to read a Buddha image without presenting mudras as a specifically Sinhala invention.
